execution: REPLAY against the venue's time-and-sales tape; NOT account executions

decisions.stage: 1  ENTRY -- is this market worth quoting at all?
decisions.label: REPLAY -- tape-priced, NOT an execution

inputs_at_decision_time.depth_at_touch: NOT OBSERVABLE in this corpus -- prices only
inputs_at_decision_time.known_at_this_instant: the book and the clock. Nothing about what the price later did.

alternatives_considered.why: the policy is two-sided; a one-sided quote is a directional bet, which is a different mandate

economics.uncertainty: whether EITHER leg fills. Across the corpus 358 of 420 episodes never filled at all (85%).

decisions.reason: the spread clears the minimum and the book is two-sided, so a paired fill is worth the spread less fees. The engine does not forecast direction; it is paid for the spread.
decisions.case_study_mechanism: Two-sided market making -- the mechanism the maker case studies describe: earn the spread and the maker rebate, avoid carrying direction.
decisions.evidence: entry rule frozen in Policy(min_spread_ticks=2); 420 episodes admitted from the corpus

decisions.stage: 2  QUOTE PLACEMENT -- where in the book?
decisions.label: REPLAY -- tape-priced, NOT an execution

inputs_at_decision_time.queue_position: NOT OBSERVABLE -- see the unsupported list

alternatives_considered.why_not: costs a tick of edge on every fill to buy queue priority that cannot be measured
better price conditional on filling, worse odds of filling; the corpus already shows fills are scarce

economics.queue_uncertainty: swept, not known: qfrac 0.00/0.25/0.50/1.00. Every fill count in this demonstration is reported at qfrac 0.25.

decisions.action: JOIN THE TOUCH on both sides
decisions.reason: the engine cannot observe queue position, so paying a tick for priority buys something unmeasurable. Joining is the only placement whose cost is known.
decisions.case_study_mechanism: Passive liquidity provision at the touch.
decisions.evidence: placement=AT_TOUCH, frozen; queue effect swept across four fractions rather than assumed

decisions.label: REPLAY -- tape-priced, NOT an execution

inputs_at_decision_time.book_depth: NOT USED -- the corpus carries none, and a rule that needed it could not be validated here

alternatives_considered.why_not: spends the same capital on a 2-tick book as on a 4-tick book

alternatives_considered.action: EDGE_SCALED -- scale by spread above the policy minimum
size to a fraction of resting depth
alternatives_considered.why_not: not computable on this corpus, so not validatable

economics.bounds: x0.50 .. x2.00 of the base clip
economics.measured_effect: IT IS AN ALLOCATION RULE, NOT A PROFITABILITY LEVER. Edge and capital both scale with the clip, so per-capital-hour is invariant to a uniform change. Measured on this corpus it cut HELD capital-hours at every queue fraction (-66 to -348) and improved per-capital-hour at three of four, but net P&L moved BOTH WAYS (+14.20 to -18.08). Four clustered observations; that is not an improvement anyone should bank.
economics.uncertainty: the sign of the net effect

decisions.action: EDGE-SCALED CLIP: 100 contracts (FIXED x1.00 -- fixed clip)
decisions.reason: a wider spread pays more for the same capital and the same queue risk, so it earns more size. Only decision-time inputs are used: the book's own spread, never a realised fill rate and never a later price.
decisions.evidence: implemented in bettor_episodes.decision_time_size; measured in acceptance/strategy_v2.json against the same baseline

decisions.stage: 4  PARTIAL FILL -- one leg filled, and only partly
decisions.label: REPLAY -- tape-priced, NOT an execution

inputs_at_decision_time.known_at_this_instant: the size that traded against us. Not whether more will follow.

alternatives_considered.why_not: it could also fill, doubling exposure before the first leg is matched

alternatives_considered.action: immediately take the other side to flatten
alternatives_considered.why_not: pays the taker fee at once for an exposure that may still be matched passively

economics.uncertainty: 43 of 60 filled episodes were partial -- a partial is the NORMAL case, not the exception

decisions.action: CANCEL THE RESTING LEG; hold 52.34 unmatched
decisions.reason: the inventory cap is half a clip. Letting the second side rest while a leg is unmatched is how a market maker becomes a directional trader by accident.
decisions.case_study_mechanism: Inventory control -- the case-study mechanism that separates market making from position taking.
decisions.evidence: note recorded on the episode: cancelled the resting leg on the first fill -- a leg filled and the other side is still working. Letting it rest while a leg is unmatched is how a market maker becomes a directional trader by accident

decisions.stage: 5  COMPLETION -- how does the unmatched leg get closed?
decisions.label: REPLAY -- tape-priced, NOT an execution

alternatives_considered.why_not: ties capital up for an unbounded time at an unknown probability

alternatives_considered.action: complete the pair as a taker
exit the leg as a taker
alternatives_considered.why_not: realises the loss and abandons the $1 pair value

economics.residual_basis: MATCHED_PAIR_PAYS_1 -- certain, but not cash until settlement
economics.uncertainty: NONE on the pair's value -- a matched pair pays exactly $1. The uncertainty is WHEN.

decisions.action: COMPLETE THE PAIR as a taker
decisions.reason: a matched pair is worth exactly $1 at settlement, which is certain. Paying the taker fee converts an uncertain directional position into a certain one.
decisions.case_study_mechanism: Pair completion / netting -- the case-study mechanism for turning a half-filled quote into a riskless holding.

decisions.stage: 6  NETTING TO CASH -- can the pair be turned into cash now?
decisions.label: REPLAY -- tape-priced, NOT an execution

inputs_at_decision_time.basis: MATCHED_PAIR_PAYS_1 -- certain, but not cash until settlement

alternatives_considered.action: merge/net the pair into cash at the venue
alternatives_considered.why: no merge or netting call has been demonstrated against this venue, and none appears in the contract we have exercised. This remains UNAVAILABLE.

alternatives_considered.action: SELL BOTH LEGS BACK -- the feasible alternative, now implemented
alternatives_considered.why: pays the spread plus two taker fees to convert a certain settlement claim into cash now. Implemented as Policy(release_matched=True) and MEASURED: it fired twice in 470 episodes, cost $1.75, and freed 26 of 3,696 held capital-hours.
on this corpus the release is not worth its cost

economics.consequence: capital-hours accrue at the full committed amount for the whole holding period, and this is the dominant term in every per-capital-hour figure in the economic verdict.

decisions.action: HOLD TO SETTLEMENT -- on measurement, not for want of an option
decisions.reason: the merge call is still unavailable, but the feasible alternative is now implemented and was measured: selling the pair back costs more than the capital it frees on this corpus. THE BINDING CAPITAL COST IS NOT HELD INVENTORY. It is collateral resting behind quotes that never fill -- 27,955 capital-hours against at most 3,696 held. Releasing pairs attacks the small term.
decisions.case_study_mechanism: Capital recycling -- alternative implemented, measured, and found not to be the constraint.

decisions.stage: 7  EXIT -- taking a loss rather than carrying a leg
decisions.label: SCENARIO -- constructed to exercise a path the corpus does not contain

inputs_at_decision_time.observed_verdict: the path FIRES but closes nothing -- the recovery window expired before size traded. The corpus does not contain a material loss-taking event.

alternatives_considered.action: keep waiting for a passive match
alternatives_considered.why_not: the recovery window expired; waiting longer is an unbounded commitment of capital at an unknown probability

alternatives_considered.action: exit the leg as a taker

alternatives_considered.why_not: only available while the opposite side is quotable; the exit path exists for when it is not

economics.observed: no material exit in this corpus

scenario.label: SCENARIO -- not observed
scenario.alternative_if_carried: unbounded until settlement; a YES that settles at 0 loses the full 73.00 USD
scenario.reading: the exit costs a known 3.43 USD; carrying risks 73.00 USD. That ratio is why the rule exists.

economics.uncertainty: the exit price. The scenario prices the exit at the opposite touch, which is the best case for a taker; a wider book costs more.

decisions.action: EXIT AS TAKER when the recovery window expires
decisions.reason: a bounded loss taken on time is cheaper than an unbounded carry. The rule is implemented and fires; its ECONOMICS are shown by scenario because the corpus never exercised them.
decisions.evidence: 2 observed taker exits, both at $0.00 realised -- reported rather than dressed up

decisions.stage: 8  HOLDING -- resting through a quiet market
decisions.label: REPLAY -- tape-priced, NOT an execution

alternatives_considered.why_not: under the incentive programme, resting time IS the product being paid for -- cancelling early forfeits qualifying uptime

economics.uncertainty: whether a fill ever arrives. 85% of episodes answer no.

decisions.reason: collateral is committed at entry whether or not a fill arrives, so a quote that never fills still costs capital-hours. That cost is counted, not ignored.
decisions.case_study_mechanism: Liquidity provision -- the shape an incentive programme pays for, and the reason C4 exists as a separate candidate.
decisions.evidence: capital-hours integrate collateral_incl_resting over every episode's own life, filled or not

decisions.stage: 9  CAPITAL REUSE -- how often can the same dollar work?
decisions.label: REPLAY -- tape-priced, NOT an execution

alternatives_considered.why: see decision 6 -- not available at this venue
measured: 2 firings, $1.75 cost, 26 capital-hours freed. Not the constraint.

economics.turnover_limit: a dollar committed to an episode cannot be committed to another until that event settles
economics.consequence: supportable turnover is bounded by settlement cadence, not by the engine's speed

decisions.reason: with no netting call, HELD capital waits for the event. But the measurement moved the diagnosis: 88% of committed capital-hours are RESTING behind unfilled quotes, not held in inventory. The binding constraint on scale is the fill rate, not the netting call.
decisions.evidence: capital-hours measured per candidate in economic_verdict.json and strategy_v2.json

decisions.stage: 10 INCENTIVE ELIGIBILITY -- does resting here earn a reward?
decisions.label: SCENARIO -- constructed to exercise a path the corpus does not contain

inputs_at_decision_time.competing_depth: NOT OBSERVABLE in this corpus -- so the rows below are a SCENARIO sweep, not a measurement

alternatives_considered.why_not: the discount factor is 0.25 per tick -- one tick back is a 75% cut to our score

economics.reading: our 100 contracts create eligibility only where the side already holds 400-499. Below that the side never reaches Target Size; far above it our share is diluted.
economics.uncertainty: TOTAL on the competing depth -- this is precisely the quantity the observation release measures.

decisions.action: REST AT THE TOUCH, and measure the depth before committing
decisions.reason: the reward is a share of a pool whose denominator is competing size. Without that number the reward cannot be computed, only bracketed.
decisions.evidence: bettor_incentive_score, pinned against the venue's own worked example (1000 at four levels, DF 0.30 -> 70.6% / 1.9%)

still_absent.status: STILL ABSENT. No merge call has been demonstrated at this venue. The feasible alternative -- selling both legs back -- is implemented and measured, and it is not a substitute: it pays the spread for capital the merge would return whole.
STILL UNOBSERVABLE. The replay sweeps a queue-ahead fraction instead of knowing one, and EVERY fill figure in this demonstration inherits that sweep.

NOT APPLICABLE, which is different from not computable. The ladder depth the reward formula needs IS in every row of this corpus. What is absent is a PROGRAMME: none of these five sports markets was observed in any incentive programme, so their reward is zero and any share figure quoted for them is a transferred scenario, not a measurement.

NOT IN THIS CORPUS AT ALL. The tape carries no close time and no event start time -- only a state transition that arrives after the fact. It is the natural input for refusing to quote into a resolving event, which is where the entire evaluation loss came from, and the observation release captures it from the incentives API.
NOT ESTABLISHABLE BY OBSERVATION. It needs our own orders in the book. No amount of watching substitutes for it.
